parsed.headline: President Mahama congratulates Brazil’s Lula on re-election

pages.text: President John Dramani Mahama of Ghana has congratulated Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva on his re-election, stating the victory offers an opportunity to deepen relations between Ghana and Brazil and strengthen cooperation among Global South countries. In a Facebook message, Mahama described the win as well-deserved and reaffirmed a commitment to advancing ties between the two nations, noting their shared history. Mahama also identified the Accra Reset initiative as a platform for the leaders to advance shared interests and development priorities for the Global South. 80-year-old Lula secured another term following a presidential runoff election on October 25, 2026, where he defeated Flávio Bolsonaro of the Liberal Party. According to results from Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court, Lula received 51.79 percent of valid votes, totaling 64,256,232 votes, while Bolsonaro obtained 48.21 percent, or 59,826,041 votes. This victory extends the tenure of the leader who previously served from 2003 to 2010 and returned to the presidency in 2023.

parsed.headline: Experts warn US climate forecasting capacity hampered by NOAA cuts amid El Niño risks

pages.text: Former government officials and scientists have warned that sweeping cuts to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) under President Donald Trump have severely hampered the United States' capacity to forecast, research, and respond to extreme weather events. These warnings come as the country faces potential hazards fueled by a potentially historic El Niño this winter. Since January 2025, the agency has lost approximately 20% of its staff. According to the reporting by The Guardian Environment, the administration has slashed staff levels, canceled contracts and grants, and shut down research laboratories and databases since the start of the president's second term. Tom Di Liberto, a former NOAA climate scientist and current media director of Climate Central, stated that the system has not been tested since the cuts occurred and questioned whether the country can handle potential coast-to-coast extremes this winter.

The National Weather Service, which is housed within NOAA, has also been affected. Across its 122 forecast offices, hundreds of technical and meteorological positions remain vacant, and weather stations have been forced to cut operating hours and delay data collection. Experts note that the internal environment at NOAA has been characterized by plummeting morale and increased burnout. This reduction in capacity coincides with a

super El Niño, a climate phenomenon involving warmer than average equatorial sea surface temperatures. The phenomenon is expected to strengthen through the northern hemisphere’s autumn and winter. Potential impacts include dangerous temperature spikes, supercharged storms in parts of the American west, and sea level rises in California of up to one foot, which could lead to flash floods, landslides, and debris flows.

parsed.headline: Ghanaian Minority calls for independent audit of South Africa evacuation payments and Minister's resignation

pages.text: The Minority in Parliament in Ghana has called for an independent investigation into payments made by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to 1,964 Ghanaians evacuated from South Africa between May 27 and September 4, 2026. During a press conference in Accra on Tuesday, October 27, the Minority demanded the resignation of Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, stating his handling of the exercise brought his office into disrepute. Samuel Abdulai Jinapor, the Ranking Member on Parliament's Foreign Affairs Committee, also called for an independent audit of evacuation exercises conducted since 2017 by an internationally reputable accounting firm to establish facts regarding alleged payment shortfalls and financial irregularities. The Minority warned it would call on President John Dramani Mahama to dismiss the Minister or initiate a vote of censure in Parliament if he does not step down. The demand follows the release of Ministry documents via a Right to Information request, which the Minority claims contain discrepancies such as gaps in flight records, inconsistencies in payment registers, duplicate entries, and missing supporting receipts. Specifically, the caucus raised concerns regarding reintegration and transport allowances, noting reports from at least three individuals who claimed they received GH¢2,000 instead of the announced GH¢5,500 support package. The Minority seeks to establish accountability for the GH¢49.72 million reportedly spent during the evacuation amid xenophobic attacks in South Africa.

Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa has denied allegations of financial impropriety, maintaining that the evacuation expenditure is fully accounted for. Speaking from Ottawa, Canada, the Minister stated that all evacuees, including minors, received the full package consisting of GH¢5,000 in reintegration support and GH¢500 for transportation. He noted that his ministry has received no complaints regarding payment shortfalls since the exercise began, and no concerns were raised at the airport regarding missing envelopes or incorrect amounts. Separately, the Minority rejected allegations made during a press conference by some evacuees on October 26, 2026, claiming that opposition figures had attempted to coach them to speak against the government. Mr. Jinapor denied that the Minority had paid or persuaded any evacuees to make these allegations, suggesting instead that individuals chose to speak out after discovering discrepancies in their received allowances.

parsed.headline: Bangladesh Prime Minister's adviser condemns obstruction of freedom fighter's burial

pages.text: Zahed Ur Rahman, the Prime Minister's Information and Broadcasting Adviser, described the obstruction of the burial of freedom fighter Manik Poshari in Pirojpur, Bangladesh, as unfortunate. Speaking at a press conference at the Secretariat on October 27, 2026, Rahman stated that those committing such acts will not receive support. Tension reportedly arose in Pirojpur on October 24, 2026, regarding a Guard of Honor for Poshari. Poshari passed away on October 24, 2026, and had previously testified in the International Crimes Tribunal against former Jamaat-e-Islami leader Delawar Hossain Sayedee regarding charges of crimes against humanity during the 1971 Liberation War.

parsed.headline: Discovery of abandoned baby orangutans in eastern India raises questions regarding wildlife trafficking

pages.text: The discovery of five baby orangutans abandoned on a plantation in eastern India has highlighted the country's role as a destination for trafficked apes, according to reporting by the Associated Press via Mongabay. Experts attribute this trend to wealthy collectors, expanding air links with Southeast Asia, and loopholes in wildlife laws. Between 2021 and 2024, India legally imported 41 orangutans, though experts have raised questions regarding the origins of those animals. Additionally, efforts to return rescued orangutans to Indonesia have stalled. Scrutiny regarding the ownership of apes intensified following the transfer of one orangutan to a private wildlife facility operated by the family of billionaire Mukesh Ambani.

parsed.headline: Japan to provide $317 million loan to Bangladesh for economic resilience and energy security

pages.text: Japan will provide a 50-billion-yen ($317 million) loan to Bangladesh to support the country's economic resilience and ensure a stable energy supply, according to a joint statement issued following a summit in Tokyo on October 27, 2026. The loan, titled “Emergency Support Loan for Enhancing Economic Resilience and Stable Energy Supply,” serves as the first yen-loan project under Japan’s Partnership on Wide Energy and Resources Resilience Asia (POWERR Asia) initiative. During the summit, Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi discussed the importance of international cooperation to strengthen oil stockpiles and improve coordination between energy-producing and energy-consuming nations in response to global energy market volatility and rising prices.

The two nations also announced a new framework titled “BIG-B for Shared Prosperity,” which builds upon Japan’s Bay of Bengal Industrial Growth Belt (BIG-B) initiative. Under this framework, the leaders agreed to collaborate on developing the Matarbari-Maheshkhali area into a logistics, energy, and industry hub centered on the Matarbari Deep Sea Port. Prime Minister Rahman arrived in Tokyo on October 26, 2026, for a four-day official visit at the invitation of Prime Minister Takaichi. The Bangladesh delegation included several officials, such as Finance and Planning Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury and State Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Anindya Islam Amit.

parsed.headline: DR Congo reports over 10,000 Ebola cases in Bundibugyo virus outbreak

pages.text: Health authorities in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) have reported 10,060 confirmed Ebola cases and 4,887 deaths since the outbreak was identified in mid-May. The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention has described the event as the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history. According to the DRC’s Ministry of Public Health, the outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo virus, a rare strain for which no approved vaccine or specific treatment currently exists. On October 23, 2026, the World Health Organization announced that the first clinical trial for a vaccine had been rolled out. Approximately 80 percent of new cases are reportedly coming from outside the chains of transmission currently being monitored by health authorities. The outbreak has been recorded in 66 health zones across eight provinces, increasing from three zones in the initial days of the outbreak. Responders in the DRC have stated that some treatment centers are overwhelmed, while remote and newly affected areas face shortages of health workers and medical supplies.

The outbreak has spread beyond the borders of the DRC. Kenya has confirmed nine infections, including two deaths, following a patient's travel from the DRC through Uganda to Nairobi. In Nigeria, authorities confirmed an infection in a Swiss woman, the wife of a Swiss diplomat, who fell ill after visiting Uganda; she has since been evacuated to Switzerland. Authorities are investigating the location where she contracted the virus. The Africa CDC has noted that at least 95 percent of cases must originate from known contacts of infected people for the outbreak to be considered under control. Ebola spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person, causing symptoms such as fever, diarrhea, and occasionally bleeding. Early symptoms may resemble malaria, which can potentially delay isolation and treatment.
